questions.question: Explain the difference between rotation and revolution.
questions.expected_answer: Rotation is a planet spinning on its axis, and for the Earth it takes about twenty-four hours, giving us day and night. Revolution is a planet travelling around the Sun in its orbit, and for the Earth it takes 365¼ days, which is one year. The Earth does both at the same time, rotating about three hundred and sixty-five times in each revolution.

questions.question: Why do we have leap years?
questions.expected_answer: The Earth takes 365¼ days to revolve around the Sun, but our calendar has only three hundred and sixty-five days, because it cannot have a quarter of a day. The extra quarter days are saved up, and after four years they add up to one whole day. So every fourth year, 29 February is added, making a leap year of three hundred and sixty-six days. This keeps the calendar in step with the Earth's journey.

questions.question: How does a planet's distance from the Sun affect the length of its year? Give two examples.
questions.expected_answer: The further a planet is from the Sun, the longer its orbit and the more slowly it moves, so the longer its year. Mercury, the closest planet, takes only eighty-eight days to go around the Sun. Neptune, the furthest, takes about one hundred and sixty-five Earth years. Mars takes nearly two Earth years and Jupiter about twelve.
